note: Practice data. Every person, ticket, chat and document here is invented for the LeakTrace demo; the vendor is fictional.

documents.title: Isolating a leak on the cooling loop
text: Purpose. This procedure covers isolating a leak on a branch of the data hall cooling loop while keeping the racks that must stay running supplied with water.

Before you plan to move any valve, read its maintenance tickets and what we already know about it. Never plan around a valve with an open failed-to-operate ticket: treat that valve as stuck until a repair ticket closes it.
Row A. Closing V-01 and V-07 cuts off the Row A branch pipe SEG-A1. Rack A1 then depends on the backup link valve V-09 being opened, because Rack A1 must keep running.
If the backup link V-09 cannot be used, do not isolate Row A on your own. Call the duty manager and agree a plan with the ML platform team, who own the training job on Rack A1.

documents.title: Opening the backup link valve V-09
text: V-09 joins the Row B side to Manifold A through the backup link pipe SEG-X1. It is normally closed.
To open it, check that Row B has spare flow, open V-09 slowly over one minute, then confirm that Rack A1 flow holds on meter FM-RA1.
The actuator on V-09 can seize after long periods closed. Exercise V-09 once a month, as listed in the maintenance schedule PM-LOOP.

documents.title: Row A cooling runbook
text: Row A holds Rack A1 and Rack A2. Rack A1 runs the model training job and inference service and must keep running. Rack A2 runs the nightly batch and can be paused.
Leak sensors LS-A1 on the Row A branch pipe and LS-A3 on the Rack A2 feed. Pressure sensor PS-MA sits on Manifold A.
A small leak on the Rack A2 feed SEG-A3 can be stopped by closing V-04 alone; the nightly batch on Rack A2 is moved first.

documents.title: Kestrel Flow Controls KF-200 actuator service note (fictional vendor)
text: KF-200 actuators that stay closed for several weeks may fail to open on the first command: the motor hums but the stem does not turn.
Fix: replace the gearbox, then run three full open and close cycles before returning the valve to service.

documents.title: Preventive maintenance schedule for the cooling loop
text: Monthly: exercise the backup link valve V-09 (open, then close). Owner: Dana Reyes.
Quarterly: exercise V-01 to V-08 and test the leak sensors LS-A1, LS-A3 and LS-B1.
Planned for next year: valve V-11 on the future Row C branch.

documents.title: On-call and ownership chart
text: The cooling operations team owns the cooling unit CDU-1, the pipes and every valve, including the backup link valve V-09. Lead: Sam Okafor. Duty manager: Alex Moreau.
The ML platform team owns the model training job and the inference service on Rack A1. On-call: Priya Nair.
The data engineering team owns the nightly batch and the dev sandbox. On-call: Jo Brandt.

tickets.title: Quarterly exercise of the Rack A1 valve
tickets.text: V-03 opened and closed normally. No action needed.

tickets.title: Leak sensor on the Rack A2 feed drifting
tickets.text: LS-A3 read wet when dry. Recalibrated and tested with a damp cloth.

tickets.title: Rack B1 valve weeping at the packing
tickets.text: Packing on V-05 tightened and replaced. No more drips.

tickets.title: Row B branch pipe inspection
tickets.text: SEG-B1 inspected along its length. No corrosion or drips.

tickets.title: Manifold A pressure sensor replaced
tickets.text: PS-MA failed its self-test and was replaced like for like.

tickets.title: Quarterly exercise of the Row B branch valve
Backup link valve failed to open on its monthly exercise
tickets.text: V-09 did not open from closed after six weeks idle. The actuator hums but the stem does not turn, as in vendor note VN-KF200. Gearbox ordered. Treat V-09 as stuck until it is repaired.

tickets.title: Quarterly exercise of the Manifold A inlet valve
Leak sensor test on the Row A branch pipe
tickets.text: LS-A1 alarmed within two seconds of a damp cloth and cleared when dry.
